name: Performance Review Checklist
description: A checklist for preparing, conducting, and following up on a performance review meeting.

items.text: Review the employee's goals from the previous cycle
Gather specific examples of work and outcomes
Collect peer or stakeholder feedback if used
Note key strengths and clear growth areas
Draft an agenda and main talking points
Send the employee the agenda and a self-review prompt
items.note: Advance notice leads to a richer conversation.

items.text: Schedule enough uninterrupted time for the discussion
Book a private, comfortable space or video room
Confirm the time and format with the employee
Have notes, examples, and the form ready to reference
Silence notifications and remove distractions
Plan an open, calm tone for the conversation
items.note: Your demeanor sets the tone for honesty.

items.text: Start by putting the employee at ease
Explain the purpose and flow of the meeting
Invite the employee to share their self-assessment first
Acknowledge their overall contributions early
Confirm this is a two-way discussion, not a lecture
Listen actively before offering your view
Review achievements against the agreed goals
Use specific examples for both wins and gaps
Balance recognition with honest growth feedback
Discuss challenges and what support is needed
Keep feedback focused on behavior and outcomes
Ask questions and check the employee's understanding
Set clear, measurable goals for the next cycle
Agree on development actions and resources
Clarify expectations and how success will be measured
Discuss career aspirations and growth paths
Confirm any commitments you are making as a manager
End on a forward-looking, encouraging note
items.note: Leave the employee motivated, not deflated.

items.text: Document the discussion and agreed goals promptly
Share written notes with the employee for alignment
File the completed review per your HR process
Schedule follow-up check-ins to track progress
Act on the support and commitments you promised
Reflect on the conversation to improve future reviews
items.note: Consistent follow-through builds trust over time.

faq.q: How do I prepare for a performance review meeting?
faq.a: Gather concrete examples of work, review goals set last cycle, collect any peer feedback, and outline talking points. Send the employee the agenda in advance so they can prepare too.

faq.q: How should I structure the review conversation?
faq.a: Open positively, review achievements against goals, discuss growth areas with specific examples, listen to the employee's perspective, then agree on goals and next steps together.

faq.q: How do I give constructive feedback in a review?
faq.a: Be specific and behavior-focused, balance strengths with growth areas, use examples rather than generalizations, and frame development as forward-looking. Make it a dialogue, not a verdict.

faq.q: What should happen after the review meeting?
faq.a: Document the discussion and agreed goals, share written notes with the employee, schedule follow-up check-ins, and act on any commitments you made so the conversation drives real change.

faq.q: Can I print this performance review checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, prepare before each meeting, and check off every step before, during, and after the conversation to keep reviews consistent and fair.
